clue.text: What may bring chilly conditions to promenade?

definitions.text: What may bring chilly conditions to promenade?

parts.words: What may bring chilly conditions to promenade?
parts.note: a weather system arriving with cold air, read playfully as a chilly seaside promenade, since a promenade is also called the front

explanation.surface: A forecaster wonders what will make the seaside walk cold.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the seafront promenade is simply 'the front', so the weather term splits into chilly plus seafront.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteorological boundary where colder air advances, bringing a drop in temperature.

clue.text: Up at Cambridge say. (advanced level)

definitions.note: performing up in front of the audience at the Cambridge, a London West End theatre

parts.note: on means advanced or forward, as in getting on
a stage is a level or phase reached

explanation.surface: A student is up at Cambridge university, studying at an advanced level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up at Cambridge' looks like university residence, but the Cambridge is also a London theatre; an actor up there is performing.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor appearing at a theatre such as the Cambridge is performing before an audience.

clue.text: Clear up rank that is more messy

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word clear read from bottom to top

parts.note: to clear a place is to rid it
a tier is a rank or row

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up a row of seats that has become untidier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear up' looks like tidying, but 'up' turns RID into DIR; 'that is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirtier is the comparative of dirty, meaning grubbier or more untidy.

clue.text: Access account coming from Thirsk, for example

indicators.note: the letters for account come out of the word for the Yorkshire venue

parts.note: Thirsk is a horse racing track in North Yorkshire, an example of a racecourse

explanation.surface: Someone gives an account of how to get to Thirsk.
explanation.walkthrough: Thirsk is a small Yorkshire town with a racecourse; removing AC ('coming from') leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Having recourse to something means having access to it as a source of help.

clue.text: Design for macintosh?

parts.note: macintosh reads as a raincoat, but a Macintosh is a member of the Scottish clan, which has its own woven check pattern

explanation.surface: A fashion designer plans a pattern for a raincoat.
explanation.walkthrough: A mac is a British raincoat; the lower-case spelling hides the Scottish clan Macintosh, whose checked pattern is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish clan's distinctive woollen check pattern is its clan design.

clue.text: Given commission from three card trick

indicators.note: a trick here is a manipulation, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conjurer's three-card trick earns them a commission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three card trick' is a familiar con, but 'trick' signals that THREE and CARD are rearranged; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chartered body is one granted a royal charter, a formal commission to act.

clue.text: Flap used in banking lire on a new order

indicators.note: putting the letters into a new order is rearranging them

explanation.surface: A bank changes the lire it holds into a fresh arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banking' suggests money, helped by 'lire', but it is an aircraft tilting in a turn; 'new order' rearranges LIRE into ILER, with A before and ON after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged surface on an aircraft wing that tilts it when the plane turns.

clue.text: Lewdness shown in no prim modes, typically?

indicators.note: the answer is shown in the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Lewd behaviour is the opposite of prim modes of conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans 'prIM MODES TYpically'; the surface hints that prim people would never behave so.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodesty is lack of decency, the indecent quality of lewd behaviour.

clue.text: Has time to convert such disbelief

indicators.note: converting is changing form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A missionary has time to convert someone who doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert' suggests religion, apt for disbelief, but it signals rearranging HAS and TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheism is disbelief in any god.

clue.text: One leaves historic ruins, yet one cannot fly

indicators.note: the letter for one is to be left out of the anagram fodder
ruins means the remaining letters are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone walks away from historic ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I ('One') out of HISTORIC ('leaves') and rearrange the rest ('ruins').
explanation.definitionFit: The large African bird is flightless.

clue.text: Weapon carried by tube

parts.note: tube suggests the London Underground, but a submarine fires its self-propelled missile from a tube

explanation.surface: A commuter carries a weapon on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's Underground; here it is the launching tube of a submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater missile is launched from a submarine's tube.

clue.text: Mary embraces John in Spain, in grass

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside, so one name goes within the other

parts.note: Maria is a form of the name Mary
Juan is the Spanish form of John

explanation.surface: Mary hugs John while they lie on Spanish grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Spain' belongs to John; 'in grass' is a link plus definition. Grass is slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is slang for cannabis, the drug made from hemp leaves.

clue.text: Stone Age artefact used in hotel management

indicators.note: management means handling or arranging, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prehistoric stone tool turns up in a hotel's manager's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Management' signals rearranging IN and HOTEL; 'used' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A neolith is a stone implement from the later Stone Age.

clue.text: Cover for a balloonist

parts.note: cover suggests insurance or protection, but it is the fabric bag that holds the hot air of a balloon

explanation.surface: Someone takes out insurance cover for a balloon pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests insurance; the answer is a covering, also the gas bag of a balloon.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabric bag of a hot-air balloon is called by the same word as a paper wrapper for letters.

clue.text: Suit area in Hertfordshire

indicators.note: in signals that the letter for area goes inside the county name

parts.note: Herts is the standard abbreviation for Hertfordshire, a county north of London

explanation.surface: A property in some area of Hertfordshire is under consideration.
explanation.walkthrough: Hertfordshire is an English county north of London, shortened to HERTS.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four sets in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Hard lines on budget for farming

annotationWithheld.why: Hard lines on budget for farming: HUSBAND (budget) + RY (lines) gives the whole answer, leaving 'Hard' with no job; no parse uses every word
annotationWithheld.clue: Hard lines on budget for farming

clue.text: Fund-manager more certain to support rate of exchange

indicators.note: in a down clue, the second piece sits under the first, supporting it
exchange means swapping places, so the letters of rate are rearranged

parts.note: surer means more certain

explanation.surface: A financier is surer about the rate of exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate of exchange' looks like currency, but 'of exchange' rearranges RATE into TREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer looks after the money of a club or organisation.

clue.text: Anchorite engineers tricky clues

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters are twisted into another order

explanation.surface: A hermit's engineers compose tricky clues.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorite is a religious hermit who lives withdrawn from society.

clue.text: Saddest is "the most guilt-ridden

definitions.meaning: most apologetic or full of regret

explanation.surface: The unhappiest person is the one with the most guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorry means both wretched and regretful, so its superlative fits both senses.

clue.text: Rabbit on soft toy for baby

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft
a rattle is a shaken toy for an infant

explanation.surface: A soft rabbit is sitting on a baby's toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' looks like a soft toy, but 'rabbit on' is British slang for chattering endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is British slang for talking at length about trivia, as babble does.

clue.text: Screwball I toy did get broken

indicators.note: something broken comes apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An eccentric's toy got broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwball' looks like a toy, but it is the definition: an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwball is an eccentric person, a strange character or curiosity.

clue.text: Tie-break for police in game

indicators.note: in signals that the detectives go inside the animal

parts.note: deer are game, animals hunted for sport
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: A police team settles a tie in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' suggests a match, but it is hunted animals; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A decider is a final contest played to settle a tied match.

clue.text: She was ill met by moonlight. Ain't it a mix up?

definitions.text: She was ill met by moonlight.

indicators.note: mixing up means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare quote followed by a confused query.
explanation.walkthrough: In A Midsummer Night's Dream, Oberon greets the fairy queen with 'Ill met by moonlight, proud' and her name.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy queen in Shakespeare's comedy is greeted by Oberon with the words ill met by moonlight.

clue.text: Herb-Austrian composer with a word of French

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer
mot is French for word

explanation.surface: A herb named after an Austrian composer who spoke French.
explanation.walkthrough: Alban Berg was a twentieth-century Austrian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bergamot is an aromatic plant of the mint family, used as a herb.

clue.text: Raptor so upset over kill

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over the second
in a down clue, upset means the word so is turned upside down

parts.note: prey is an animal's kill

explanation.surface: A bird of prey is upset over its kill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' in a down clue turns the word upside down; 'kill' here is a noun, the animal caught.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish-eating hawk is a bird of prey.

clue.text: Expedients of Bob's. say?

definitions.meaning: quick methods of getting something done
bobs, for example, are brief haircuts

explanation.surface: Bob's ways of saving time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name, but a bob is a short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick routes or methods that save time, and also cropped haircuts.

clue.text: Negative, strange power makes bridge contract

parts.note: not is a negative
rum is British slang for odd

explanation.surface: A negative, odd power produces a deal on a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: In card bridge, a contract may be played without a trump suit; 'rum' is British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract in the card game of bridge in which no suit ranks as trumps.

clue.text: Night covers, divine in essence

indicators.note: in signals that the clergy letters go inside the word for essence

parts.note: being is essence or nature
DD is Doctor of Divinity, so a divine is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman's night coverings and the essence of something holy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: a clergyman, DD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets and blankets are the covers used on a bed at night.

clue.text: Raise siege and release

definitions.meaning: to lift a siege by sending forces to free a besieged town
to free someone from a duty or burden

explanation.surface: An army lifts a siege and frees the townspeople.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve a besieged town is to end its siege; to relieve someone is to free them.

clue.text: Most recent history of wide-eyed satyr

indicators.note: wide here suggests the letters spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A goat-legged woodland god stares in wide-eyed amazement at the latest history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wide-eyed' reads as one word, but 'wide' is the anagram indicator for EYED and SATYR.
explanation.definitionFit: The day before today is the most recent day of the past.
